title: "East Side of Prairie Ave." / "West Side of Prairie Ave." — measured-style street elevation drawing of the 1800 and 1900 blocks

notes: Two strips of flat front elevations drawn to a common scale. WEST SIDE (south→north, left→right): 1936 Allerton, 1912, 1906, 1900 Keith | 1834 Jones (two-storey with a mansard and central tower-dormer — consistent with the 1886 mansard addition), 1828 Shipman (small mansard), 1824 (large gabled stone front with bay — the Marsh refacing), 1816 Henderson (mansard with dormers), 1812 Wheeler (scrolled Flemish gable, round attic window), 1808 Keith (latticed parapet), 1800 Glessner (long, low, at far right). EAST SIDE (north→south, left→right as seen from the street): 1801 Kimball (château) with low service wing, 1811 Coleman (gable, arched entry), 1815 Sears/Meeker (mansard with gables), 1823 Dent (mansard), 1827 Doane (twin towers), then 1901, 1905 Field, 1919, 1923, 1945. Identification of each elevation is this researcher's reading from position and style (not captioned). Glessner House blog (2011, "Business Encroachment on Prairie Avenue") says the drawing "shows the 1800 and 1900 blocks of Prairie Avenue as they appeared at the time" of a 1914 Daily News article; author and date of the drawing are not stated — it looks like a modern reconstruction. The ONLY elevation-scale evidence found for 1816, 1823, 1824, 1828 and the post-1886 1834. Same drawing recorded by the 1900 stream from the blog (a19-gh-prairie-1800-1900-elevations). NOTE: the streetscape stream records the same chicagology image as st-chicagology-prairie-elevation-strips (no building ids); this record is kept for its per-house identification — merge the two.
